title.en: Orbit rig that follows a moving subject until the user takes over

summary: Orbit the camera around a subject with damping and clamped limits, tween focus over 0.9 s, keep following a moving character, and hand control back the moment the user drags.
objective: A viewer can watch a moving character from behind without the camera fighting them: the follow stops on the first drag, the framing never falls inside geometry, and one reset returns the home pose.
intent_signals: make the camera follow the character
the camera keeps fighting my mouse
orbit around the model but let me stop it
chase camera for the moving vehicle
example_prompts: Follow a walking character from behind while the user can still orbit.
Give the drone a chase camera that snaps back to the overview.
Frame a moving robot arm and stop following as soon as I drag.
negative_signals: fixed cinematic camera path with no user input
not_for: Cutscene camera animation where the user has no control at all.
First-person walk-throughs, which need collision and head height rather than an orbit pivot.

principles: The camera is a second pair of hands: any tween or follow that keeps moving while the user drags reads as a broken control, so the first user gesture cancels both.
Clamped polar angles and a distance range are what keep the frame legible; without them a viewer can end up under the ground plane or inside the subject and conclude the scene is broken.
Damping is a readability choice, not smoothing for its own sake: it separates the subject's motion from the camera's, so the eye keeps tracking the subject.
A follow is a pivot update, not a path. Move the orbit pivot with the subject and let the offset the user chose ride along; animating a bespoke curve fights every user input.
One named home pose makes exploration safe, because the viewer knows a single action returns to a frame that reads.
implementation: Create OrbitControls(camera, canvas) and set enableDamping true and enablePan false so the pivot stays on the subject.
Clamp with minPolarAngle and maxPolarAngle (25 deg to 85 deg here) and with minDistance / maxDistance (2.5 m to 18 m), converting degrees with THREE.MathUtils.degToRad.
Tween the camera position and the controls pivot together over 0.9 s with a smoothstep ease so the move starts and ends calmly; see templates/rigs/camera-orbit-follow.js.
While a follow function is set, add the subject delta to both the camera position and the orbit pivot each frame; the offset the user chose is preserved.
Subscribe to the OrbitControls 'start' event and clear both the tween and the follow there; that single listener is the whole hand-back rule.
Return a boolean from update(dt) that is true while the tween or follow is live, so an on-demand render loop keeps drawing only while something moves.
Keep the first entry of the views map as the home pose and implement reset as setView(home), which also cancels any tween.
observable_checks: Dragging during a focus tween stops the tween immediately and the camera stays where the drag left it.
Orbiting to the extremes never places the camera below the ground plane or closer than the minimum distance, at any viewport aspect.
With the subject moving, the on-screen size and screen position of the subject stay roughly constant until the user drags.
Reset returns to the same home pose from any position, and the render loop goes idle afterwards.
Nothing in the scene moves or changes state because of a camera action.

creative_affordances: Limits, tween duration and ease are style choices: a snappier 0.4 s or a slower 1.4 s move both work as long as the cancel-on-input rule survives.
The follow can lead the subject, sit off to one side, or hold a fixed compass bearing instead of the offset the user left.
known_limits: Authored camera-behaviour guidance; no runtime or perceptual measurement was performed for these numbers.
No occlusion test is described: the rig can still pass through geometry between the camera and the subject unless the scene adds its own handling.

defaults.rationale: Limits and timings tuned against templates/rigs/camera-orbit-follow.js: 25-85 deg polar keeps the camera above the ground and off the pole, 2.5-18 m spans a close inspection and a full establishing frame for a human-scale subject, and the 0.9 s smoothstep focus reads as deliberate without feeling slow. The damping factor and the cancel-on-input rule matter more than any single number.

focus.cancel_on: OrbitControls 'start' event clears the tween and the follow

follow.keeps: the orbit offset the user last chose
follow.stops_when: the user drags, or the caller clears the follow function

reset.pose: first entry of the views map

never: a follow that continues while the user is dragging
an unclamped polar angle that lets the camera go under the floor
moving the subject to suit the camera
